fixes.explanation: Yes, friend, cities with pasturelands around them. The LORD tells Moses to have Israel give them from the inheritance the people will possess (Numbers 35:2). The Levites get homes and room for their herds and flocks. That fits what the LORD told Aaron earlier, that the Levites would have no inheritance in the people's land (Numbers 18:20). So the other tribes share what they have, and the Levites aren't left out.

I get the guess, since Moses is speaking on the plains of Moab across from Jericho (Numbers 35:1). But the LORD never names a valley for the Levites. He asks for cities to live in and pasturelands around them, given from the inheritance of the tribes (Numbers 35:2). One big valley would be easier to hand over, but that's not the order. It's cities, spread out.

Worship makes sense, friend. The Levites are the ones who perform the work of the Tent of Meeting (Numbers 18:23). But for these six cities, the LORD names a different purpose. They are appointed as cities of refuge, a place a manslayer may flee to (Numbers 35:6). So the word that fits the blank is refuge.

Yes, the assembly. The LORD says the cities are a refuge from the avenger, so the manslayer will not die until he stands trial before the assembly (Numbers 35:12). The city is where he is kept safe from the avenger in the meantime. The assembly is the group that will hear his case.

Good guess, friend, but prophets aren't named in this verse. The LORD says the manslayer stands trial before the assembly (Numbers 35:12). A few verses later, the congregation is the one told to judge between the slayer and the avenger of blood (Numbers 35:24). So the people are the ones doing the judging. I'd say that's a lot of responsibility for a crowd.

Yes, even a bare hand can do it. The verses just before this one name an iron object, a stone and a wooden object (Numbers 35:16-18). Then verse 21 adds that if in hostility someone strikes another with his hand and he dies, the one who struck him must surely be put to death, and he is a murderer. So no tool is needed in that case. It's a heavy part, and the text is clear.

Careful here, friend. The earlier verses do list an iron object, a stone and wood (Numbers 35:16-18). But verse 21 goes on to say that if in hostility someone strikes another with his hand and he dies, he is a murderer who must surely be put to death. So a hand in hostility counts too. That makes this one True.

That's it, friend. This is the case where the killing was not done in hostility. The assembly is to protect the manslayer from the hand of the avenger of blood (Numbers 35:25). After that, the assembly returns him to the city of refuge he fled to. He lives there until the death of the high priest.

The text goes the opposite direction, friend. For the one who killed by accident, verse 25 says the assembly is to protect him from the avenger of blood (Numbers 35:25). Nothing there has the assembly giving him up. Then he is returned to the city of refuge he fled to. So the assembly stands between him and the avenger.

That's the reason the text gives. Then the LORD says, “Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.” (Numbers 35:34) The land matters because He lives among His people. That's a wonderful thing to be told. Now I feel like keeping my own bakery extra clean.

Other nations aren't mentioned in this verse, friend. The LORD gives a different reason: “Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell. For I, the LORD, dwell among the Israelites.” (Numbers 35:34) The reason is that He lives among His people there. That's what is at stake, and it isn't about what anyone else might hear.
